BURSEVI:v10p316#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p316#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p316#2/r1.claim: The greater fire can mean the lowest, hottest layer of Hell, where Pharaoh's people, hypocrites, and those who rejected Jesus' table are placed.
BURSEVI:v10p316#2/r1.anchor: أي يدخل الطبقة السفلى من طبقات النار

BURSEVI:v10p316#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p316#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p316#2/r2.claim: Another interpretation compares the great fire of the afterlife with the lesser fire of this world, which is only one seventieth of Hell's fire.
BURSEVI:v10p316#2/r2.anchor: وقيل الكبرى نار جهنم والصغرى نار الدنيا يعني إن المفضل نار الآخرة

BURSEVI:v10p316#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p316#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p316#2/r3.claim: The author prefers the greater punishment of the Hereafter, with worldly and barzakh punishment as the lesser punishment.
BURSEVI:v10p316#2/r3.anchor: يقول الفقير : الظهر إن المراد بالنار الكبرى هو العذاب الأكبر

BURSEVI:v10p316#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p316#2/r4.speaker: بعض الحكماء
BURSEVI:v10p316#2/r4.claim: A sage lists gluttony, excessive sleep, persistent sin, hardness of heart, forgetting God, and facing the Almighty as signs of wretchedness.
BURSEVI:v10p316#2/r4.anchor: قال بعض الحكماء علامة الشقاوة أشياء كثيرة الأكل والشرب والنوم والإصرار على الذنب

BURSEVI:v10p316#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p316#2/r5.speaker: النجمي
BURSEVI:v10p316#2/r5.claim: The Najmiyya reading calls worldly attachment to desires the lesser fire and describes the afterlife's greater fire as abandonment, loss, expulsion, and estrangement.
BURSEVI:v10p316#2/r5.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : النار ناران نار حجاب الدنيا بالاشتغال بالشهوات والذات وهي الصغرى

BURSEVI:v10p317/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p317/r1.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p317/r1.claim: Al-Qashani describes greater fire as veiling from God through association and attachment, divine coercion in attributes, wrath in acts, and enduring punishments across four spiritual realms.
BURSEVI:v10p317/r1.anchor: وقال القاشاني : النار الكبرى هي نار الحجاب عن الرب بالشرك والوقوف مع الغير

QASHANI:87:12/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:87:12/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:87:12/r1.claim: The most wretched is one veiled from the Lord, lacking readiness and spiritually distant, worse than the prepared person whose readiness has lapsed and who is veiled by the dark qualities of the self.
QASHANI:87:12/r1.anchor: المحجوب عن الرب، العديم الاستعداد، النائي القلب

QASHANI:87:12/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:87:12/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:87:12/r2.claim: The great fire is the fire of veiling from the Lord by associating others and stopping at them, then fires of coercion, wrath, and the effects of hell through four stations from dominion to divinity, lasting forever; the second person experiences only the fire of effects.
QASHANI:87:12/r2.anchor: التي هي نار الحجاب عن الرب بالشرك والوقوف مع الغير، ونار القهر في مقام الصفات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p285/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p285/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p285/r10.claim: The description of burning in the great fire clarifies the otherwise vague label most wretched in this early Meccan period.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p285/r10.anchor: لأن إطلاق { الأشقى } في هذه الآية في صدر مدة البعثة المحمدية فكان فيه من الإبهام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p286/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p286/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p286/r2.claim: Calling the Fire the greatest heightens warning and threat; it means Hell.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p286/r2.anchor: ووصف النار ب { الكبرى } للتهويل والإنذار والمراد بها جهنم .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p741/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p741/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p741/r8.claim: The greater fire may be the lowest layer of Hell, or Hell itself contrasted with the lesser fire of this world.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p741/r8.anchor: السفلى من أطباق النار وقيل { الكبرى }

MUQATIL:87:8-13/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:87:8-13/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:87:8-13/r5.claim: The one already known by God's prior knowledge as wretched enters the Great Fire, which is Hell.
MUQATIL:87:8-13/r5.anchor: قد سبق علم الله فيه بالشقاء الذي

NASAFI-FULL:v4p333/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333/r1.claim: He enters the great Fire, identified as Hell; the lesser fire is the fire of this world.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333/r1.anchor: يدخل نار جهنم والصغرى نار الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:87:11-13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:11-13/r2.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:87:11-13/r2.claim: Al-Farraʾ says the greatest fire is the lowest of Hell’s levels.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:11-13/r2.anchor: وهي السفلى من أطباق النار قاله الفراء

QURTUBI-FULL:87:11-13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:11-13/r3.speaker: الحسن ويحيى بن سلام
QURTUBI-FULL:87:11-13/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and Yahya ibn Sallam identify the greatest fire as Hell and the lesser fire as the fire of this world.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:11-13/r3.anchor: وعن الحسن: الكبرى نار جهنم، والصغرى نار الدنيا وقاله يحيى بن سلام.

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.claim: Al-Aʿla is Meccan and has nineteen verses; the Prophet loved it, recited it at Eid and Friday prayers with al-Ghashiya, sometimes on the same day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.anchor: سورة الأعلى مكية وآياتها تسع عشرة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.claim: The surah turns the entire cosmos into a sanctuary reverberating with praise and offers the Prophet good news of divine preservation and ease in his mission and affairs.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.anchor: وحق لرسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أن يحب هذه السورة وهي تحيل له الكون كله معبدا

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.claim: Its foundations are God's oneness as creator, divine revelation, and afterlife recompense, rooted in earlier scriptures; it also portrays the easy nature of the message, messenger, and community.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.anchor: وهي تتضمن الثابت من قواعد التصور الإيماني

QUTB-ZILAL:87:10/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:10/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:10/r1.claim: The Prophet fulfills his duty by reminding; people then diverge in response and outcome, and God deals with them according to how they receive the reminder.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:10/r1.anchor: فإذا نهض [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] بهذا العبء فقد أدى ما عليه

QUTB-ZILAL:87:12/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:12/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:12/r1.claim: The great Fire is Hell, great in intensity, duration, and vastness, where the wretched person remains for a long time.

STUDYQURAN:87:12/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:12/r1.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:87:12/r1.claim: The greatest Fire is the Hereafter's Fire, contrasted with the lesser fire of this world.
STUDYQURAN:87:12/r1.anchor: The “greatest” or “greater” Fire is that of the Hereafter, while the lesser fire is that of this world

STUDYQURAN:87:12/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:12/r2.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:87:12/r2.claim: Alternatively, the verse distinguishes degrees of punishment, with the worst Fire destined for the most wretched.
STUDYQURAN:87:12/r2.anchor: Alternately, v. 12 alludes to different degrees of punishment, with the greatest Fire being that for which the most wretched are destined

TAB-FULL:v24p317/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p317/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p317/r2.claim: Qatāda says God-fearing people remember, while anyone who avoids the reminder out of contempt for it and its people is wretched.
TAB-FULL:v24p317/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {فذكر إن نفعت الذكرى سيذكر من يخشى} [الأعلى: 10] فاتقوا الله، ما خشي الله عبد قط إلا ذكره

TABATABAI:87:14-16/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r7.claim: The apparent meaning of the greatest fire is Hell, greater than worldly fire; an alternative identifies it as Hell’s lowest and most painful level.
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r7.anchor: الظاهر أن المراد بالنار الكبرى نار جهنم وهي نار كبرى بالقياس إلى نار الدنيا

TABATABAI:87:14-16/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r8.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r8.claim: An alternative interpretation takes the greatest fire to be Hell’s lowest, most painful level.
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r8.anchor: وقيل المراد بها أسفل دركات جهنم وهي أشدها عذابا

TABRISI:87:10-17/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:10-17/r4.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:87:10-17/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the greater fire is Hell, while the lesser fire is the fire of this world.
TABRISI:87:10-17/r4.anchor: والنار الصغرى نار الدنيا عن الحسن

TABRISI:87:10-17/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:10-17/r5.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:87:10-17/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ identifies the greater fire as Hell's lowest level.
TABRISI:87:10-17/r5.anchor: النار الكبرى هي الطبقة السفلى من جهنم عن الفراء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r5.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r5.claim: The greatest fire is the immense, terrifying fire.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r6.claim: It is greater and hotter than the fire of this world.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r6.anchor: قال: مقاتل: لأنها أعظم وأشد حرا من نار الدنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r7.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r7.claim: It is the lowest level of Hell, whose fire is especially great and hot.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r7.anchor: وقال الكلبي: هي النار السفلى (¬9). يعني أن نار تلك الطبقة

WAHIDI-QT:87:12/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:87:12/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:87:12/r1.anchor: { الذي يصلى النار الكبرى } الذي يدخل جهنم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r8.anchor: الذي يصلى النار الكبرى } الذي يدخل جهنم.

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:12:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:12:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:12:anmerkung/r1.claim: The construction ṣaliya plus fire as object is common in early Quranic descriptions of the afterlife.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:12:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Das Verb ṣaliya + nār (oder ein Synonym dafür) als Objekt ist ein häufiger Bestandteil bereits frühkoranischer Jenseitsbeschreibungen

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r1.claim: The second stanza again addresses the messenger: he first praises God, perhaps with close followers, then speaks to a wider audience with an admonition that makes verse 6’s revelation public in purpose.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r1.anchor: Das zweite Gesätz beginnt wie das erste mit einem Aufruf an den Verkünder

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r4.claim: Verses 10–11 contrast good and bad responses to proclamation; verse 11 expands the bad response with a conventional warning of Hell, balanced by the promise to the good in verses 14–15.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r4.anchor: Auf den das zweite Gesätz einleitenden Aufruf folgt in V. 10.11 eine Antithese

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r5.claim: The passage forms a chiasm: the responses of good and bad in verses 10–11 correspond to their fates in verses 12–15, as in Q 92:5–11 and 14–21.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r5.anchor: Zusammen mit der an den Guten gerichteten Verheißung V. 14.15 ergibt sich eine chiastische Struktur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r6.claim: The statement that the condemned neither die nor live conveys eternal, horrific punishment: they persist, but their suffering is no positive form of life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r6.anchor: Cehennemdekiler ölmezler, yaşarlar; ancak çektikleri dikkate alındığında bunun olumlu anlamıyla yaşamak olmayacağı da muhakkaktır

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#3/r1.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#3/r1.claim: Al-Farraʾ says “the greatest Fire” is the lowest layer of Hell; Alusi sees no difficulty in Hell having levels that differ in size and heat.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#3/r1.anchor: أي الطبقة السفلى من أطباق النار كما قال الفراء ولا بعد في تفاضل نار الآخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#3/r2.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#3/r2.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the greatest Fire as the afterlife's Hellfire and the lesser fire as worldly fire; a marfuʿ report from Abu Hurayra says earthly fire is one seventieth of Hellfire, while an Ahmad version says one hundredth, perhaps using seventy as an expression of great number.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#3/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن الكبرى نار الآخرة والصغرى نار الدنيا ففي الصحيحين عن أبي هريرة مرفوعا ناركم هذه جزء منسبعين جزءا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401#3/r1.claim: The ‘greatest fire’ is immense and dreadful, hotter and more severe than the fire of this world.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401#3/r1.anchor: العظيمة والفظيعة، لأنها أعظم وأشد حرا من نار الدنيا

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:9-12/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:9-12/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:9-12/r5.claim: The “greatest Fire” is Hell, since the Prophet said earthly fire is one seventieth of Hellfire; an alternative identifies it with Hell's lowest pit.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:9-12/r5.anchor: ناركم هذه جزء من سبعين جزأ من نار جهنم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p399/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p399/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p399/r4.claim: The most wretched person plunges heart and body into the greatest fire, understood as Hell's lowest level because he is hard-hearted through ignorance, blind imitation, or arrogant defiance.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p399/r4.anchor: أعظم الطبقات وهي السفلى لأنه ليس في طبعه أن يخشى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p399/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p399/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p399/r5.claim: Alternatively, the greatest fire is the afterlife fire, seventy times greater than the fire of the intermediate realm and the present world.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p399/r5.anchor: نار الأخرى فإنها أعظم من نار البرزخ وأعظم من نار الدنيا بسبعين جزءا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p399/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p399/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p399/r6.claim: The passage uses ellipsis by correspondence: fear and happiness in the first group imply the omitted hard-heartedness and misery of the second, while the second group's cause and outcome imply the first group's opposites.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p399/r6.anchor: ذكر الثمرة في الأول وهي الخشية دليلا على حذف ضدها من الثاني

BIQAI-FULL:v8p399/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p399/r7.speaker: الملوي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p399/r7.claim: Al-Mulawi says Quranic eloquence pairs cause and outcome across passages, avoiding repetition; he illustrates decree, execution, and allocation through the planning and operation of a waterwheel.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p399/r7.anchor: قال الملوي : ولا شك أن القرآن العظيم على أحسن ما يكون

BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r8.claim: The purification, remembrance, and prayer reprise the opening's divine traits: removing defects and acquiring perfections; this paired ellipsis links prayer with escape from the greatest fire.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r8.anchor: وكان متخلقا بما ذكر من أخلاق الله في أول السورة

TAB:87:12/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:12/r1.speaker: author
TAB:87:12/r1.claim: The person enters Hell, the greater fire, called greater because of its intense heat and pain.
TAB:87:12/r1.anchor: الذي يَرِد نار جهنم ، وهي النار الكبرى ، ويعني بالكبرى لشدّة الحرّ والألم

NASHR:v2p112/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p112/r6.speaker: أصحاب التفريق بين رؤوس الآي وغيرها
NASHR:v2p112/r6.claim: Some soften lām at verse endings for euphony and emphatically pronounce it elsewhere because of the preceding trigger; Ibn al-Jazari cites this as a preferred distinction.
NASHR:v2p112/r6.anchor: فرققوها في رءوس الآي للتناسب وغلظوها في غيرها لوجود الموجب قبلها

NASHR:v2p112/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p112/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p112/r7.claim: The verse-final examples are fa-la saddaqa wa-la salla, wa-dhakara isma rabbihi fa-salla, and idha salla; non-final examples include yasla al-nar.
NASHR:v2p112/r7.anchor: فلا صدق ولا صلى في القيامة وذكر اسم ربه فصلى في سبح إذا صلى في العلق

ABUHAYYAN:87:12/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:12/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:12/r1.claim: The verse describes the outcome awaiting the evildoer in the afterlife: entering the great fire.
ABUHAYYAN:87:12/r1.anchor: ثم وصفه بما يؤول إليه حاله في الآخرة ، وهو صلي النار ووصفها بالكبرى .

ABUHAYYAN:87:12/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:12/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN:87:12/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the great fire as the fire of the afterlife and the lesser fire as the fire of this world.
ABUHAYYAN:87:12/r2.anchor: قال الحسن : النار الكبرى : نار الآخرة ، والصغرى : نار الدنيا .

ABUHAYYAN:87:12/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:12/r3.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN:87:12/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the great fire is the lowest level among Hell’s layers.
ABUHAYYAN:87:12/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء : الكبرى : السفلى من أطباق النار .

ABUHAYYAN:87:12/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:12/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:87:12/r4.claim: Another view says the fire of the afterlife has gradations, with some parts greater than others.
ABUHAYYAN:87:12/r4.anchor: وقيل : نار الآخرة تتفاضل ، ففيها شيء أكبر من شيء .

ALUSI:87:12/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:12/r1.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI:87:12/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ identifies the “greatest fire” as the lowest layer of Hell; al-Ālūsī sees no problem in the afterlife fire having different sizes and intensities.
ALUSI:87:12/r1.anchor: أي الطبقة السفلى من أطباق النار كما قال الفراء ولا بعد في تفاضل نار الآخرة وكون بعض منها أكبر من بعض وأشد حرارة

ALUSI:87:12/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:12/r2.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI:87:12/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the greatest fire is the fire of the afterlife, while the lesser fire is the fire of this world.
ALUSI:87:12/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن الكبرى نار الآخرة والصغرى نار الدنيا

ALUSI:87:12/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:12/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI:87:12/r3.claim: Abū Hurayra reports from the Prophet that the worldly fire is one part in seventy of Hell’s fire.
ALUSI:87:12/r3.anchor: ففي الصحيحين عن أبي هريرة مرفوعاً ناركم هذه جزء من سبعين جزءاً من نار جهنم

ALUSI:87:12/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:12/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI:87:12/r4.claim: Another Prophetic report from Abū Hurayra, transmitted by Aḥmad, says the worldly fire is one part in one hundred of Hell’s fire; al-Ālūsī suggests seventy may be an expression of abundance.
ALUSI:87:12/r4.anchor: وفي رواية للإمام أحمد عنه مرفوعاً أيضاً أن هذه النار جزء من مائة جزء من جهنم فلعل السبعين وارد مورد التكثير

BAGHAWI:87:12/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:12/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:87:12/r1.claim: The “great fire” is tremendous and dreadful because it is hotter and more intense than the fire of this world.
BAGHAWI:87:12/r1.anchor: العظيمة والفظيعة ، لأنها أعظم وأشد حراً من نار الدنيا .

BAYDAWI:87:12/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:12/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:12/r1.claim: The greater fire is Hell; the Prophet says the worldly fire is one part in seventy of Hell's fire, or it is the lowest level of Hell.
BAYDAWI:87:12/r1.anchor: نار جهنم فإنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ناركم هذه جزء من سبعين جزءا من نار جهنم

BIQAI:87:12/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:12/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:12/r1.claim: The condemned person directly and completely endures the fire, suffering in heart and body.

BIQAI:87:12/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:12/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:12/r2.claim: One explanation is that this is the greatest, lowest layer of the fire: its inhabitant does not fear and is as hard as stone through blind imitation or arrogant defiance.
BIQAI:87:12/r2.anchor: كالجلمود الأقسى لأنه جاهل مقلد أو متكبر معاند

BIQAI:87:12/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:12/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:12/r3.claim: Alternatively, al-nār al-kubrā is the hereafter's fire, seventy degrees greater than the fire of the intermediate realm and this world.
BIQAI:87:12/r3.anchor: بسبعين جزءاً ، فلهذا استحقت أن تتصف بأفعل التفضيل على الإطلاق

BIQAI:87:12/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:12/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:12/r4.claim: The verses use interwoven omission: fear, the fruit of happiness, implies its omitted opposite hardness, while the misery named as a cause implies omitted happiness; this encourages the first and warns against the second.
BIQAI:87:12/r4.anchor: وهي الخشية دليلاً على حذف ضدها من الثاني

BIQAI:87:12/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:12/r5.speaker: الملوي
BIQAI:87:12/r5.claim: Al-Malawī explains the Qurʾān's concision: one passage gives a consequence without its cause, another the cause without its consequence, and each implies the other, as do decree, ordainment, and judgment.
BIQAI:87:12/r5.anchor: قال الملوي : ولا شك أن القرآن العظيم على أحسن ما يكون

BIQAI:87:12/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:12/r6.speaker: الملوي
BIQAI:87:12/r6.claim: Al-Malawī illustrates the interdependence of judgment, decree, and ordainment with a waterwheel: design is planning and judgment, construction is decree, and measured distribution of water is ordainment.
BIQAI:87:12/r6.anchor: قال الملوي : ولا شك أن القرآن العظيم على أحسن ما يكون

BIQAI:87:15/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:15/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:15/r7.claim: A second interwoven omission links the fire mentioned first with its omitted opposite in the next verse, and the purification named next with its omitted opposite earlier; purification, remembrance, and prayer figure in a therapy sequence.
BIQAI:87:15/r7.anchor: من الاحتباك في الاحتباك : ذكر أولاً الصلى دليلاً على حذف

IBNASHUR:87:12/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:12/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:12/r1.claim: Calling the Fire al-Kubra magnifies its terror as a warning; it refers to Hell.
IBNASHUR:87:12/r1.anchor: ووصف النار ب { الكبرى } للتهويل والإنذار والمراد بها جهنم

IBNATIYYA:87:12/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:12/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:12/r1.claim: The condemned person is destined to suffer the Fire.
IBNATIYYA:87:12/r1.anchor: ووجب له صلي النار ، وقال الحسن

IBNATIYYA:87:12/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:12/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA:87:12/r2.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the greater Fire as the Fire of the afterlife and the lesser fire as the worldly fire.
IBNATIYYA:87:12/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن : " النار الكبرى " نار الآخرة ، والصغرى نار الدنيا

IBNATIYYA:87:12/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:12/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNATIYYA:87:12/r3.claim: Some commentators say the afterlife's Fire has degrees of severity, with some parts greater than others.
IBNATIYYA:87:12/r3.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين : إن جميع نار الآخرة وإن كانت شديدة فهي تتفاضل ، ففيها شيء أكبر من شيء

IBNATIYYA:87:12/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:12/r4.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA:87:12/r4.claim: Al-Farra says “the greater” means the lowest layer of Hell.
IBNATIYYA:87:12/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء : الكبرى هي السفلى من أطباق النار

KASHSHAF:87:12/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:12/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:12/r1.claim: Al-nar al-kubra is the lowest layer among Hell's layers.
KASHSHAF:87:12/r1.anchor: { النار الكبرى } السفلى من أطباق النار

KASHSHAF:87:12/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:12/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF:87:12/r2.claim: Another view identifies al-kubra as Jahannam.

KASHSHAF:87:12/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:12/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:12/r3.claim: The lesser fire is the fire of this world.

MAWARDI:87:12/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:12/r1.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI:87:12/r1.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam identifies the greater fire as Hell and the lesser fire as the fire of this world.
MAWARDI:87:12/r1.anchor: هي نار جهنم ،   والصغرى{[3247]} نار الدنيا ،   قاله يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI:87:12/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:12/r2.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI:87:12/r2.claim: Al-Farra’s interpretation identifies the greater fire as the disbelievers’ fire in Hell’s lowest level and the lesser fire as sinners’ fire in its upper level.
MAWARDI:87:12/r2.anchor: الكبرى نار الكفار في الطبقة السفلى من جهنم ،   والصغرى نار المذنبين في الطبقة العليا من جهنم ،   وهو معنى قول الفراء

NASAFI:87:12/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:12/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:12/r1.claim: The ‘great fire’ is Hell, while the lesser fire is the fire of this world.
NASAFI:87:12/r1.anchor: يدخل نار جهنم والصغرى نار الدنيا

QURTUBI:87:12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:12/r1.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:87:12/r1.claim: Al-Farra identifies the great fire as the lowest of Hell's layers.
QURTUBI:87:12/r1.anchor: وهي السفلى من أطباق النار . قاله الفراء

QURTUBI:87:12/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:12/r2.speaker: الحسن ويحيى بن سلام
QURTUBI:87:12/r2.claim: Al-Hasan and Yahya ibn Sallam identify the great fire as Hell and the lesser fire as the fire of this world.
QURTUBI:87:12/r2.anchor: وعن الحسن : الكبرى نار جهنم ، والصغرى نار الدنيا

RAZI:87:12/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:12/r1.speaker: الحسن
RAZI:87:12/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the “greatest fire” is Hell, contrasted with the lesser fire of this world.

RAZI:87:12/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:12/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:87:12/r2.claim: Another view holds that the afterlife has fires and levels of differing severity, matching the varying gravity of sins; the worst unbelievers enter the greatest fire.
RAZI:87:12/r2.anchor: أن في الآخرة نيرانا ودركات متفاضلة كما أن في الدنيا ذنوبا ومعاصي متفاضلة

RAZI:87:12/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:12/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:87:12/r3.claim: A third view identifies the greatest fire with the lowest level, where unbelievers suffer, as stated of hypocrites.
RAZI:87:12/r3.anchor: أن النار الكبرى هي النار السفلى

RAZI:87:12/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:12/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:87:12/r4.claim: Some say the verse was revealed about al-Walīd, ʿUtba, and Abī; Rāzī says the wording applies generally, especially since the sequence is rationally established.
RAZI:87:12/r4.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في الوليد وعتبة وأبي

RAZI:87:12/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:12/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:87:12/r5.claim: Rāzī notes that the mention of the most wretched alongside those who remember and fear raises the question whether a lesser wretched group must exist.
RAZI:87:12/r5.anchor: إن الله تعالى ذكر ههنا قسمين

RAZI:87:12/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:12/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:87:12/r6.claim: One answer is that a superlative need not imply an actual comparative, as in the verse calling the people of Paradise better settled and rested.
RAZI:87:12/r6.anchor: أن لفظة الأشقى لا تقتضي وجود الشقي إذ قد يجري مثل هذا اللفظ من غير مشاركة

RAZI:87:12/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:12/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:87:12/r7.claim: Another proposed answer takes “the most wretched” simply as “the wretched one who burns,” like “easier” meaning “easy” in another verse.

RAZI:87:12/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:12/r8.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
RAZI:87:12/r8.claim: An unnamed poet’s use of “more honored” and “taller” illustrates superlative forms without an implied rival.
RAZI:87:12/r8.anchor:
مثل قول القائل :
إن الذي سمك السماء بنى لنا *** بيتا دعائمه أعز وأطول

RAZI:87:12/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:12/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:87:12/r9.claim: Rāzī’s preferred account distinguishes the knowledgeable, the hesitant, and the obstinate: the knower is happy, the hesitant has some misery, and the obstinate who ignores the call is most wretched.

FARRA:v3p256/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p256/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p256/r11.claim: The great fire is the lowest of Hell's layers.

NAHHAS:v5p205/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p205/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p205/r17.claim: The great fire is Hell; al-Farra specifies the lowest layer of Hell.
NAHHAS:v5p205/r17.anchor: قال جهنم وقال الفراء السفلى من أطباق النار

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r1.claim: The Prophet should not pursue the obdurate or force the message: he is to remind when useful, while the fearful heed it and the wretched evade it and face their fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r1.anchor: The Prophet (sws) is directed not to go after the stubborn and the obdurate.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p278/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p278/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p278/r6.claim: The verses distinguish those who heed the warning from those who evade it; their rejection reflects their own condition, not a flaw in the message or preacher.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r1.claim: Evaders treat this life as all that exists and fear no Hereafter; they face eternal Fire, neither living nor dying, and will wish in vain for death.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r1.anchor: They regard this life to be all that there is.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r3.claim: The succeeding sūrah al-Ghāshiyah elaborates the same warning; its great torment and this passage's great Fire refer to the same punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r3.anchor: Both refer to the same thing in slightly different styles

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the greatest fire is the fire of the afterlife, while the lesser fire is that of this world.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r1.anchor: قال الحسن: النار الكبرى: نار الآخرة، والصغرى: نار الدنيا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r2.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ identifies the greatest fire as the lowest of Hell's levels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء: الكبرى: السفلى من أطباق النار.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r3.claim: Another view says afterlife fires differ in intensity, with some greater than others.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r3.anchor: وقيل: نار الآخرة تتفاضل، ففيها شيء أكبر من شيء.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r5.claim: Hasan says the great Fire is the Fire of the Hereafter, while the lesser one is the fire of this world.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن: النار الكبرى نار الآخرة، والصغرى نار الدنيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r6.claim: Some exegetes say the Hereafter's Fire itself has degrees, with some portions greater than others.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r6.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين: إن نار جميع الآخرة وإن كانت شديدة فهي تتفاضل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r7.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r7.claim: Al-Farra identifies the great Fire as the lowest of Hell's levels.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r7.anchor: وقال الفراء: الكبرى هي السفلى من أطباق النار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380#2/r1.claim: The Prophet says those destined to remain in Hell neither die nor live; those God will remove are made charcoal, then emerge in groups and sprout after contact with Paradise’s rivers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380#2/r1.anchor: إن أهل النار الذين يريد الله إخراجهم يميتهم فيها إماتة، حتى يصيروا فحما، ثم يخرجون ضبائر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir links the report to verses saying Hell’s inhabitants are not killed and their torment is not eased.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380#2/r2.anchor: {لا يقضى عليهم فيموتوا ولا يخفف عنهم من عذابها} [فاطر:36] إلى غير ذلك من الآيات

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r19.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r19.claim: The greatest fire is Hell, while the lesser fire is the fire of this world.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r19.anchor: هي نار جهنم , والصغرى نار الدنيا , قاله يحيى بن سلام .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r20.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r20.claim: Al-Farra says the great fire is the lowest layer of Hell for unbelievers, and the lesser fire is the upper layer for sinful believers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r20.anchor: الكبرى نار الكفار في الطبقة السفلى من جهنم , والصغرى نار المذنبين في الطبقة العليا من جهنم

THALABI:v10p184/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p184/r9.claim: The wretched enters the greatest Fire, with no death for relief and no beneficial life.
THALABI:v10p184/r9.anchor: ثم لا يموت فيها فيستريح ولا يحيى أي حياة تنفعه
